newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela suspends charges against tanker owner.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela suspends charges against tanker owner.

text.p: Venezuela's attorney general suspended charges on Thursday against the owners of the Greek oil tanker Nissos Amorgos after it supplied guarantees to pay damages for an oilspill in February.

In an interview with a local television station Globovision, Juan Nepomuceno Garrido said the owners had guaranteed payments up to 80 billion bolivars ($165 million) while the Ministry of Environment put current costs at 60 billion ($124 million).

Officials at the International Tanker Owners Pollution Compensation Fund had previously said the tanker owner's strict liability extended only to $7.2 million, with additional funds up to a total of $83 million provided by a special fund, called "Fund 71".
"There is no reason to continue with the charges when our only prescription, which was to be compensated for damages to the country, is covered by the guarantees," he said.
The Nissos Amorgos ran aground in Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo shipping channel on February 28, spilling at least 25,000 barrels of crude oil, according to official estimates.
The tanker and its captain were detained by the authorities pending an investigation into the incident.
International tanker owners organisation Intertanko had complained that the detention contravened international treaties to which Venezuela was signatory.
The spill caused protests by local fishermen who filed a separate suit against the Nissos owners for $130 million, which Intertanko said had risen to $292.5 million.
Venezuela has also detained another tanker, the Maltese-flagged Plate Princess, after it spilled up to 20 barrels of oil in the Lake Maracaibo last month.
The Maracaibo channel is Venezuela's main oil export route, carrying about 70 percent of its exports to world markets.
